conclusion: Why I believe in Chegg’s next chapterI believe in Chegg. Debt retirement, cash generation through restructuring and the emerging skilling business give me reasons to be optimistic about its reinvention. The company has already made tangible progress in reshaping its financial position. Its next opportunity is to turn that progress into a more focused learning business with recurring demand, productive investment and a cost base its revenue can support. The calculations in this case make that path measurable. My conviction is that Chegg can build on the reset it has achieved and create a stronger business for the next chapter of learning and work.
heading: Why I believe in Chegg’s reinvention.
opening: I believe in Chegg. I believe it can build a stronger future around learning and workforce skilling, and the financial progress it has already made gives that conviction a concrete foundation. Chegg retired its remaining convertible debt in September 2026 and generated positive operating cash flow through the first half of a difficult restructuring. S4 S2The opportunity is to turn that financial reset into a business that can invest in its own growth. Lower capital spending improved free cash flow, and skilling offers a direction for the next stage. This case explains why I am optimistic, what the reported numbers establish, and how disciplined reinvestment can support the transition. The cash bridge and stress test make the conditions behind my belief visible.
